title: What the Agentic AI Foundation's rule changes mean for anyone building on MCP or A2A
key_facts: The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) is a Linux Foundation body that hosts the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent2Agent (A2A) and other open source agent projects.
AAIF co-founder and CTO Manik Surtani described the changes in a keynote at AGNTCon Europe + MCPCon Europe in September and in an interview afterwards.
AAIF has existed for two years, has more than 270 member organisations (170 at its April update) and seven working groups.
Entry criteria had been modelled on the Cloud Native Computing Foundation's, which Surtani says a two-year-old field cannot meet.

AAIF now has three project stages: sandbox, growth and impact; sandbox has a six-month check-in and a 12-month review, and AAIF may open a conversation about archiving a project with no signs of life after a year.
Working groups, until recently open only to member organisations, are now open to everyone; only members can propose new groups and provide resources.
AAIF has committed to publishing yearly numbers of projects accepted, promoted and archived.
Members increasingly ask about security, identity and authentication for agents rather than governance structure.
quote_evidence: Everything's new in this space. Everything's early. It's not the CNCF.
AAIF now has three stages instead of two: sandbox, growth, impact.
For an open source community, that was a bit silly. We want everyone to participate in this stuff.
why_it_matters_hint: Open agent standards now have an easier path in and open working groups, which affects who can shape MCP and A2A.
